targets.title: The cross-national association of gun ownership rates and suicide rates: An analysis of 194 nations.
targets.evidence_quote:
Given these concerns, I reproduce the study in Kleck (2021). In addition, I attempt a
replication with analytical modifications and US state data.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
The main analysis in Kleck (2021), which used Small Arms Survey for firearm availability
estimates, showed no association between firearm availability and suicide rates. I was unable
to reproduce this result, finding instead a significant and positive association.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
In contrast to Kleck, global analyses with Small Arms Survey data found a significant and
positive association between firearm availability and total suicides, as did US analyses.
Analyses with other firearm availability measures comported with the original study, finding
no association.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Reconstructs the original public-source data and methods and obtains substantively different numbers. Alternative transformations and subgroup analyses qualify the original no-association claim; added US data are not used to settle robustness.

targets.title: The Effect of Firearms on Suicide.
targets.evidence_quote:
Using a Poisson
regression with the data in Kleck (2018, Table 17.3), I compared lethality of firearm (258,386 deaths, 308,623
attempts, 83.7% lethal) and hanging/suffocation suicide attempts (118,072 deaths, 154,013 attempts, 76.7%
lethal). Firearm suicide attempts are 8.8% more deadly, or conversely, hanging/suffocation attempts are 36.0%
more surivavable (both p < 0.001).

reasoning: DOI resolves to OSF zugae version 1; exact title and Lane authorship verified in full preprint and OSF API. Main activity reconstructs and reanalyses original public data, with additional US-sample replication. The independently analysed 2018 chapter is a second target; review criticisms alone are excluded. Reconstructed global data contain 203 rather than 194 units, an explicit limitation.
